canonical_statement: Let T be a first-order theory in a countable language. If T is categorical, with model existence, in one uncountable cardinal, then T is categorical, with model existence, in every uncountable cardinal.
domain_and_universes: universes u v w; L : FirstOrder.Language.{u,v}; T : L.Theory; source and target cardinals in Cardinal.{w}; Prop in universe 0

definition_policy.language_countability: L.card <= Cardinal.aleph0, where mathlib L.card is the supremum of the cardinalities of all function- and relation-symbol types
definition_policy.categoricity: HasModelCardinality L T kappa and Cardinal.Categorical kappa T
definition_policy.model_existence: there exists a nonempty bundled T.ModelType in universe w with Cardinal.mk exactly kappa
definition_policy.uniqueness: mathlib Cardinal.Categorical: every two bundled T-models of cardinality kappa are nonempty-isomorphic as L-structures
definition_policy.completeness: not added as a separate hypothesis

killed: changed strict uncountable domain to include aleph0
moved the theory binder beneath a uniform source-categoricity premise
changed the conclusion to categoricity at the countable boundary

status_boundary: This freezes and kernel-elaborates the exact intake-selected target, its explicit nonvacuous categoricity convention, an existential-source transport, four structural mutations, and two boundary probes. It provides no proof of Morley's theorem and no dependent-node evidence.
